Every state change is one shape changing size, the way the Dynamic Island does it. The bar animates its real width and height with springs generated from Apple's own spring equations, so the corners stay round at every frame and the text never stretches. It overshoots slightly as it grows and settles without a bounce as it shrinks. The old content blurs out while the new content sharpens in, a beat after the shape starts moving.

IslandBar

IslandBar is the save bar that floats at the bottom of a page while there's something to save. It's a dark pill that reads “Unsaved changes · Discard · Save ⌘S”. It rises from a small dot below the page and stretches sideways to fit its content, then shrinks back into the dot when there's nothing left to save.

Saving shrinks the pill to a spinner. It stays there for at least 400ms so a fast save never flickers, then a check draws itself next to Saved and the bar leaves after 1.4 seconds. If the save fails, the pill widens into the error with Try again and Discard, and the draft is untouched. Edit during the Saved moment and it goes straight back to Unsaved changes.

When someone tries to leave with unsaved changes, call nudge(). The bar swells for a moment, the Save button rings, and screen readers hear why. useIslandBar wires most of this for you: it tracks the async save, binds ⌘S or Ctrl+S, asks the browser before the tab closes, and gives you guard() for links. With reduced motion turned on, the bar only fades: sizes snap and nothing bounces.
